source.prompt: (the gray squirrel's) A western gray squirrel (Sciurus griseus), single adult standing on all fours, side-on neutral pose, legs straight under the body, head level, tail held straight out behind and slightly raised, fully fluffed. Realistic proportions: 55 cm long, half of it tail; slim body; large rounded ears with no ear tufts. Silver gunmetal-grey back and flanks, pure white belly and chin with a sharp flank line, no brown or orange anywhere. Very long broad flat bushy tail, grey with a black inner band and a white fringe. Dark eye with a thin pale eye ring. No base, no ground. Game-ready, symmetric.

tiers.note: lod0 = body + tail (12 sides x 12 rings, 288) + eyes and ear tufts (40); lod1 = body + tail (8 x 8, 144); lod2 = body + tail (4 x 5, 40). GLB 267,440 bytes.

rig: Rodent template, exactly as client/assets/squirrel.glb (tools/build_squirrel.py) and to be loaded with its loader constants: BODY 0 (hindquarters), CHEST 7 (pivot at the lumbar), HEAD 6 (neck, head, ears; pivot at the base of the neck) and LEG_A 1 (fore pair, elbows) children of the chest, LEG_B 2 (hind pair, stifles), TAIL 3 (pivot at its root) and TAIL_TIP 8 (child of the tail, pivot 0.42 along it). Parts and weights from the same geometric regions as the gray squirrel's (scaled with the body). extras.rig keys: kind, chest, tail, tail_tip, head, fore, hind, length_m. No skin.
accuracy_notes: Reads as a chickaree: a small, compact tree squirrel with a dark olive-brown back and crown, a rusty tinge down the mid-back, bright orange-buff throat, chest, belly, inner legs and feet, a black flank line between them, a pale buff eye ring, small ears with short dark winter tufts, and a narrower, flatter tail than the gray squirrel's (dark brown above, a black band near the edge, a pale rim of white-tipped hairs, rusty below). Still the gray squirrel's body: the pose, the haunch and the slim head are a Sciurus's, a chickaree is chunkier with a shorter face (the muzzle is only 0.92x). The black flank stripe is the one-face-wide border of the orange underside along the flank line, so it is jagged and continues a little onto the lower thigh; the real stripe is a clean line, bolder in summer. Seen side-on, the tail's pale rim shows as a light streak along its middle (the flattened plume is edge-on). Ear tufts on lod0 only (the dark tip is painted on every tier). The summer coat (brighter orange below, no tufts) would be a second colour set.
